_note: Question bank for Ask the Control Tower. Each entry maps a suggested question to fact-store keys; the engine assembles answers ONLY from fact-store.json values. Drafted Oct 24, 2026; gap figures updated to the settled 16.4 on Oct 26, 2026.

questions.question: What's the Pell graduation gap?
questions.template: For the 2015 entering cohort, {equity_headline.pell_rate}% of Pell recipients earned a credential within eight years, vs {equity_headline.nonpell_rate}% of non-Pell students — a {equity_headline.gap_pp}-point gap. The typical single institution's own gap is smaller: {equity_headline.median_institution_gap_pp} points at the median.

questions.citation: Gradient-boosted model of 150% graduation rate; SHAP feature importance, test period 2021–2023.
questions.question: What predicts graduation most?
questions.template: First-year retention, by a wide margin. In the lab's model it carries more than four times the weight of the next factor (SHAP {model.top_predictor_shap} vs {model.second_predictor_shap} for private nonprofit control). Institutions that keep their first-years graduate them.

questions.citation: Model trained 2015–2019, tested out of sample 2021–2023 (2020 excluded), 5,389 test institutions.
questions.question: How accurate is the model?
questions.template: It predicts an institution's 150% graduation rate to within about {model.mae_pp} points on average (MAE {model.mae_pp} pp, R² {model.r2}), tested out of sample — against {model.naive_baseline_mae_pp} points for a naive baseline.

questions.citation: 8-year award rates by institution, latest cohort; public IPEDS data.
questions.question: How does UNC Wilmington compare to the national picture?
questions.template: UNC Wilmington's Pell students finish at {spotlights.uncw.pell}% within eight years vs {equity_headline.pell_rate}% nationally, and its Pell gap is {spotlights.uncw.gap_pp} points — less than half the national {equity_headline.gap_pp}. It sits in the mainstream-middle peer cluster.

questions.citation: Cohort-weighted 150% graduation rates pooled 2015–2023; median institution-level Pell gaps by sector.
questions.question: Which sector graduates the most students — and which has the smallest Pell gap?
questions.template: Private nonprofits lead on completion ({by_sector.grad_private_nonprofit}%), then publics ({by_sector.grad_public}%), then for-profits ({by_sector.grad_for_profit}%). The smallest median Pell gap is in for-profits ({by_sector.gap_for_profit} points) — not an equity win: completion there is low for everyone.

questions.citation: Median institution-level 150% graduation and retention rates, 2015 vs 2023.
questions.question: Has graduation improved over time?
questions.template: Yes — the median four-year institution's 150% graduation rate rose from {trends.grad_2015}% in 2015 to {trends.grad_2023}% in 2023. Retention, oddly, barely moved: about {trends.retention_range} the whole period.

questions.citation: Award rates at 4, 6 and 8 years after entry, latest cohort.
questions.question: Does giving students more time close the Pell gap?
questions.template: No. Between years 4 and 8, Pell completion rises {equity_by_horizon.pell_gain} points and non-Pell {equity_by_horizon.nonpell_gain} — both groups gain, and the gap barely moves: {horizons.gap_4} points at year 4, {equity_headline.gap_pp} at year 8.

questions.citation: Cluster medians from the lab's four-cluster peer grouping of four-year institutions.
questions.question: What do peer institutions look like?
questions.template: Four clusters: small access colleges ({clusters.small_access.grad}% graduation, {clusters.small_access.pell}% Pell), large access-serving institutions ({clusters.large_access.grad}%, {clusters.large_access.pell}% Pell), the mainstream middle ({clusters.mainstream.grad}%, {clusters.mainstream.pell}% Pell), and selective, well-resourced colleges ({clusters.selective.grad}%, {clusters.selective.pell}% Pell). Similar missions, very different resources and outcomes.

questions.citation: Median institution-level 150% graduation rates by race/ethnicity, 2023.
questions.question: How big are the racial graduation gaps?
questions.template: In 2023, median graduation rates were {race.asian}% for Asian students, {race.white}% White, {race.hispanic}% Hispanic, and {race.black}% Black — a White–Black gap of {race.gap_wb} points.

questions.citation: Panel coverage: full IPEDS panel vs four-year analysis set, 2015–2023.
questions.question: How much data is this based on?
questions.template: The full panel covers {scope.full_institution_years} institution-years from {scope.full_institutions} institutions, 2015–2023. The predictive analysis uses the four-year subset: {scope.analysis_institution_years} institution-years from {scope.analysis_institutions} institutions with cohorts of 50 or more.

trustee_summary.citation: Headline findings, IPEDS Outcomes Lab panel, 2015–2023.
trustee_summary.text: Across 8,670 colleges, whether students finish depends most on whether they come back for year two. Low-income (Pell) students finish at 45.9% vs 62.2% for others — a 16.4-point gap that extra time does not close. Graduation rates are improving nationally (47.1% → 52.4% median), and the model can predict an institution's rate to within 7.15 points on average. Every figure here is federal IPEDS data, cited.
